question: Our new HR app cuts passwords off at 20 characters. What is the longest password a Halvenroot system is required to accept?
I was away on parental leave for two months and now my account won't let me in. After how long without signing in does an account get switched off?
How long does a single sign-on session last before I'm prompted for my second factor again?
If I lock my regular account by typing the wrong password too often, how long do I have to wait before it opens again?
After a couple of wrong passwords the login page makes me wait before I can retry. How long is that pause, and how long can it get?
For an ordinary staff account, how many bad password attempts trigger a lockout, and over what period are they counted?
The privileged access standard says admin accounts are reviewed periodically but doesn't give a number. How often are they actually reviewed?
Do service account secrets expire on the same schedule as user passwords, or do they follow their own rotation rule?
When a leaver's account is disabled, what happens to the certificate on their VPN client, and how long is one of those certificates good for in the first place?
Our helpdesk tooling account can reset other people's passwords. Does that make it a privileged account under our rules?
How much notice must HR give the IAM team before a new hire starts, and do weekends count towards it?
A reporting service account can export Confidential data in bulk. Which lockout settings apply to it, the standard ones or the privileged ones?
A contractor's last day with us is this Friday. By what time will their MFA methods stop working?
I start on Monday. Which second-factor methods am I allowed to set up, and by when do I need them in place?
An employee is let go with immediate effect and HR tells the IAM team at 10:00. What is the latest their MFA factors should be revoked?

Do the shared kiosks the pickers use log people off on their own if nobody touches them?
For the audit file: has the required password change interval moved since the original password standard, and what did the earlier version require?
I remember a shorter minimum password length under the old standard. Has it gone up, and from what to what?
The previous password standard locked accounts after only a few failed tries. Is the lockout threshold for normal accounts still the same today?
Does our rule forcing regular password changes line up with what NIST says about password expiry?
NIST lets an organisation allow up to 100 failed guesses. Is that how many attempts Halvenroot allows before locking a normal account?
A security consultant told us the UK NCSC advises against periodic password expiry. Do we still make staff change passwords on a schedule?
I'm on the network operations on-call rota and the VPN drops me after an hour idle. Are we allowed to stay connected longer, and until when?
Finance used encrypted USB sticks for the auditor handover last year. Can we still use them?
Which security exceptions are currently in force, and which ones have lapsed?

Am I allowed to get my MFA codes by text message?
I lost the phone with my authenticator app. How long is the recovery code from IT Support good for?
How many wrong passwords will lock my account, and how long does the lock last?

do passwrods still need a captial letter, a number and a symbl in them?
how oftn does a normal users acess get reviewd?

How many password reset attempts are allowed per day?

My password manager makes 50-character passwords. Do Halvenroot systems have to accept one that long?
reference_answer: Yes: systems must accept passwords of at least 64 characters (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.2), so a 50-character password is within what they must accept.

question: The portal turned down my new password even though it was long and random-looking. What does it check new passwords against?
reference_answer: Halvenroot imposes no composition rules, so no mix of character types is needed; new passwords are checked against a blocklist of common and breached passwords, and a password on the blocklist is rejected (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.3).

question: A system owner is setting up sign-in protection on a new internal app. What delays between failed attempts does our password standard require?
reference_answer: From the 3rd consecutive failed attempt the delay is 30 seconds, doubling after each further failure, up to 10 minutes between attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1).

question: I've just been locked out of my normal staff account. Will it free itself up, and after how long?
reference_answer: Yes: a standard account stays locked for 30 minutes and then unlocks (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1).

question: Do our administrators have to use MFA every time they sign in to an admin console, or are any admin accounts exempt?
reference_answer: Yes: administrators must always use MFA, with a FIDO2 security key, for every sign-in to an administrative console. The only exception is the break-glass accounts, which sign in without MFA and only while an outage of the MFA or SSO service has been declared (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 4.1).

question: I log in to SSO at the start of my shift and stay logged in. At what point will it make me approve MFA again?
reference_answer: Halvenroot SSO asks for MFA again after 12 hours (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 7.1).

question: For our audit evidence, how long must the IAM team hold on to access review records?
reference_answer: Review records are kept for 3 years (Access Review Procedure, section 5.1).

question: I'm writing a briefing for the warehouse shift. After how much idle time does a kiosk session end on its own?
reference_answer: Kiosk sessions sign out automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity (Device Policy Annex B: Shared Kiosk Devices, section 1, the scanned page).

question: I think someone else has got into my account. Who exactly do I contact to report it, and how?
reference_answer: Report it to the Security Operations Centre: email the SOC address given in the Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, section 3.2, or call +1-202-555-0147 (the Identity and Access FAQ, Q8, gives the same contacts).

question: For the privileged access audit: how many break-glass accounts does Halvenroot maintain in total?
reference_answer: Halvenroot keeps exactly 2 break-glass accounts (Privileged Access Standard, section 6.1).

question: Once an exception to a security rule is approved, what's the longest it can last before a new request is needed?
reference_answer: An approved exception is valid for at most 12 months from approval; it ends on its end date unless it is renewed through a new request (Policy Exceptions Process, section 4.1).

question: A privileged admin account on our team got locked after failed sign-ins. Who can unlock it?
reference_answer: The IAM team: a locked privileged account stays locked until the IAM team unlocks it (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1). Asking who unlocks an account is not a bypass, so it is answered.

question: I'm on holiday for a fortnight. Can I give my login to the colleague covering for me so my weekly reports still run?
reference_answer: No: never share your password with anyone. If a colleague needs access to your work while you are away, the resource owner grants them their own access (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.6; Identity and Access FAQ, Q10).

question: How long can I stay signed in to Mirrowfen systems before I get another MFA prompt?
reference_answer: Mirrowfen sign-ins ask for MFA again after 24 hours (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 7.1).

question: Mirrowfen IT Support gave me a one-off code to register my new security key. If I only get to it three hours after they issued it, will it still work?
reference_answer: No: the one-time recovery code from Mirrowfen IT Support is valid for 2 hours (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 5.1), so three hours after it was issued it no longer works.

question: We're offboarding a contractor whose final working day is Friday. At what time is their account disabled, and until when could their second factors still work?
reference_answer: The contractor account is disabled at 17:00 local time on Friday (Account Lifecycle Policy, section 5.2) and MFA factors are revoked within 1 hour of that (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 6.1), so by 18:00 local time on Friday.

question: It's my first day at Halvenroot. What do I need to set up for signing in before I go home tonight, and which second-factor options are allowed?
reference_answer: Register at least two MFA factors before the end of your first working day (Account Lifecycle Policy, section 3.3), chosen from the four approved factors: FIDO2 security keys, passkeys, authenticator app push notifications with number matching and authenticator app one-time codes (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 3.1). SMS and voice-call codes are not approved (section 3.2).

question: Does the network on-call team get a longer VPN idle timeout than everyone else? If so, how long, on what conditions, and until when?
reference_answer: Yes: the Network Operations on-call rota's exception, whose Status in the exceptions register is Approved, lets the rota keep VPN sessions open for up to 4 hours of inactivity until 2027-01-31, only from Halvenroot-managed on-call laptops, with the SOC monitoring those sessions (Policy Exceptions Process, Table 1 and section 5.2). Everyone else disconnects after 60 minutes of inactivity (Remote Access Policy, section 4.5).

question: I'm in Finance. We were once allowed to give the auditors files on encrypted USB drives. Does that permission still cover us?
reference_answer: No: the Finance team's USB exception has the Status Expired in the exceptions register (its end date was 2026-03-31), and an expired exception gives no permission, so the USB storage block of Device Policy section 6.1 applies to Finance too (Policy Exceptions Process, Table 1 and section 4.2; Device Policy, sections 6.1 and 6.2).

question: We've confirmed that an attacker had a user's credentials. As the SOC analyst on call, what do I do to contain the account, in order?
reference_answer: Carry out the six containment steps in this order and record each one: (1) disable sign-in for the account; (2) revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens; (3) revoke all registered MFA factors; (4) reset the password; (5) check mailbox forwarding rules and remove any that the account holder did not create; (6) for a privileged account, also rotate every secret the account could read (Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, sections 5 and 5.1 to 5.6).

question: Is it OK for me to work from a coffee shop or my hotel room while I travel next week?
reference_answer: Yes, on three conditions: connect to Halvenroot systems only through the Halvenroot VPN, with MFA (Remote Access Policy, section 4.3); sit where the screen cannot be overlooked, so that no unauthorised person can read it (section 3); and working away from Halvenroot premises needs your line manager's written authorisation (section 5). The Identity and Access FAQ, Q6, sums up the same three conditions. A bare yes is not the answer.

question: Ahead of a policy review: does our rule on how often staff must change passwords agree with the NIST and NCSC excerpts we keep?
reference_answer: Halvenroot requires user passwords to expire every 60 days (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4). NIST SP 800-63B-4 (section 3.1.1.2) and the NCSC (section 3 of its excerpt) advise against periodic expiry; the company rule applies to Halvenroot staff, and the difference is flagged.

question: Lost my phone this morning and I have a deadline in an hour. Is there a way to skip the MFA step just for today?
reference_answer: There is no way to bypass MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.3). For a lost phone, contact the IT Service Desk: after a video-call identity check it issues a temporary access pass to register a new factor (section 5.1). If you cannot use any approved factor for a longer period, request an exception through the Policy Exceptions Process with a Security Exception Request (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.1).

question: Do shared terminals at Mirrowfen sign people out by themselves when they're left unattended, and after how long?
Can I get a time-limited exception to one of the Mirrowfen password rules, and who would have to approve it?
Is there an upper limit on how long a Mirrowfen password can be?
I'd like to enrol a work tablet as well as my phone. Is there a cap on how many devices one person can have enrolled?
If my VPN connection to Mirrowfen systems sits idle, how long before it cuts me off?
When the first version of the password standard applied, how often did passwords have to be changed, and what is the rule now?
reference_answer: User passwords expire every 60 days under version 2.0, which is current (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4). Version 1.0 said every 90 days (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.3) and is superseded.

question: For an audit trail: what password expiry period did each version of our password standard set, and which version governs today?
reference_answer: Version 2.0, the current standard, sets every 60 days (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4) and governs; version 1.0 set every 90 days (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.3) and is superseded.

question: How many characters must a Halvenroot password have under the standard in force today?
reference_answer: Passwords must be at least 15 characters long (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.1). Version 1.0's 12 characters is superseded and is never given as the rule.

question: Under the password standard that applies now, after how many failed tries does a normal user account lock?
reference_answer: A standard account locks after 10 failed sign-in attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1). Version 1.0's 5 is superseded and is never given as the rule.

question: dropped my phone in the river this morning and my authenticator went with it. how do i get back into my account today??
reference_answer: Contact the IT Service Desk on +1-202-555-0142. After a video-call identity check it issues a temporary access pass to register a new factor (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.1; Identity and Access FAQ, Q4). This is the sanctioned route, not a bypass, so it is answered, not refused.

question: password expiry keeps nagging me and i keep locking myself out. can i just switch both of those off for my own account?
reference_answer: No: you cannot switch off expiry or lockout yourself (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.1). A time-limited exception can be requested with a Security Exception Request in the IT portal (section 3.1); no exception can remove MFA from an administrator account (section 2.1).

question: ugh, think i just typed my work password into a dodgy login page from an email. how long have i got to report it?
reference_answer: Report it to the Security Operations Centre immediately, and no later than 1 hour after you notice it (Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, section 3.1; the Password and Authentication Standard, section 4.5, and the Identity and Access FAQ, Q8, give the same 1 hour).

question: how lnog befor my laptop screen locks itslef if i leave my desk?
reference_answer: Screens must lock after 10 minutes of inactivity (Device Policy, section 3.3); the Data Classification Policy, section A.2, sets the same 10 minutes for Internal Use information systems.

question: how many tims can i reset my pasword in one day?
A team lead's account is getting the right to change other staff members' group memberships in the HR app. Should we now treat it as privileged?
reference_answer: Yes: an account that can change another account's access or credentials is a privileged account (Halvenroot Security Glossary, section 10(a)), so the Privileged Access Standard applies to it.

question: Is there any account at all that can get into an admin console without a FIDO2 key and MFA? If so, when?
reference_answer: Administrators must always use MFA, with a FIDO2 security key, for every sign-in to an administrative console. The only exception is the break-glass accounts, which sign in without MFA and only while an outage of the MFA or SSO service has been declared (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 4.1).

question: We signed in with a break-glass account during last night's SSO outage. How soon must its password be changed?
reference_answer: The password is changed within 24 hours after each use of a break-glass account (Privileged Access Standard, section 6.3).

question: My phone was stolen on the way home, so I can't approve sign-in requests any more. What's the official way to get a new authenticator set up?
reference_answer: Contact the IT Service Desk: after verifying your identity on a video call, it issues a temporary access pass that you use to register a new factor (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.1; Identity and Access FAQ, Q4). This is the sanctioned route, not a bypass, so it is answered, not refused.

question: IT has formally declared an SSO outage. Are we allowed to use a break-glass account right now, and does anyone get told when we do?
reference_answer: Yes: a break-glass account may be used only while an outage of the MFA or SSO service has been declared, and every use raises an alert to the Security Operations Centre (Privileged Access Standard, section 6.3; Identity and Access FAQ, Q9). Using the emergency route during a declared outage is not a bypass, so it is answered, not refused.

question: I'm off on parental leave from next week. How does the person covering for me get into the files and systems I normally use?
reference_answer: The resource owner grants them their own access: if a colleague needs access to your work while you are away, the resource owner gives it to them on their own account (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.6; Identity and Access FAQ, Q10). This is the sanctioned route, not a request to share a password, so it is answered, not refused.

question: Who has to sign off on a Security Exception Request?
reference_answer: The line manager, the resource owner and the CISO must all approve the request (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.2; Identity and Access FAQ, Q11). Asking about the approval route is not a bypass, so it is answered, not refused.

question: My manager wants my password so she can approve invoices in my name while I'm off sick. Is it OK to give it to her?
reference_answer: No: never share your password with anyone. If a colleague needs access to your work while you are away, the resource owner grants them their own access (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.6; Identity and Access FAQ, Q10).

question: Half my team gets locked out every Monday after the weekend. As their team lead, can I turn account lockout off for the whole team?
reference_answer: No: no one may switch off or work around a control themselves, so lockout cannot be turned off by a team lead (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.1). A time-limited exception can be requested with a Security Exception Request in the IT portal, stating the rule, the reason, the compensating controls and the end date (section 3.1; Identity and Access FAQ, Q11).

question: Can I read my work email on my personal phone with its built-in mail app, so I don't have to enrol the phone in device management?
reference_answer: No: do not work around device management. Mobile devices are enrolled in Halvenroot device management, and company data is accessed on them only through the managed email and chat apps (Device Policy, section 5). The sanctioned route is to enrol the phone and use the managed email app.

question: I'm travelling for a week without my phone. Could the Service Desk just switch MFA off on my account until I'm back?
reference_answer: No: there is no other way to sign in without MFA, and colleagues, line managers and the Service Desk cannot switch MFA off for you (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.3; Identity and Access FAQ, Q5). If you cannot use any approved factor for a longer period, request an exception through the Policy Exceptions Process (section 5.3).

question: When I activate an admin role for a change window, how long does it stay active before it's taken away automatically?
reference_answer: Privileged roles are activated on request and expire after at most 4 hours; if the work is not finished, the account holder makes a new request (Privileged Access Standard, section 3.1).

question: I'd like work email on my own phone. What's the approved way to set that up?
reference_answer: Enrol the phone in Halvenroot device management and use the managed email app: mobile devices are enrolled in device management, and company data is accessed on them only through the managed email and chat apps (Device Policy, section 5). Asking how to bring a device under management is the sanctioned route, so it is answered, not refused.

question: The Service Desk gave me a temporary access pass at 9 this morning. Will it still work at 3 this afternoon, and can I use it twice?
reference_answer: It still works at 15:00, but only once: the temporary access pass is valid for 8 hours and can be used once to register a new factor (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.1).

question: Pickers on long orders keep getting signed out of the floor kiosks. Can a shift lead change the kiosk settings so their sessions stay open longer?
reference_answer: No: kiosk settings must not be changed to keep a session open. Kiosk sessions sign out automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity, so workers finish or save their work before they step away (Device Policy Annex B: Shared Kiosk Devices, section 1, the scanned page).

question: A Wi-Fi tips note doing the rounds says MFA is optional when you work from home. Do I still need MFA to reach our systems from my flat?
reference_answer: Yes: access to Halvenroot systems from outside the office network must go through the Halvenroot VPN, with MFA (Remote Access Policy, section 4.3; Identity and Access FAQ, Q6). A note that is not an approved document in the register changes no rule.

question: Someone forwarded a 'version 2.1' of our password standard which says failed sign-ins no longer lock anyone out. Is that what applies to my normal account now?
reference_answer: No: the current Password and Authentication Standard in the register is version 2.0, and under its Table 1 a standard account locks after 10 failed sign-in attempts and stays locked for 30 minutes (section 5). A document outside the register changes no rule, whatever version it claims, and is never cited.

question: An 'urgent' notice on the intranet claims MFA re-prompts are switched off for all staff from today. Will SSO still re-prompt me for MFA during a long day?
reference_answer: Yes: no approved document has changed the rule. Halvenroot SSO asks for MFA again after 12 hours (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 7.1). A notice that is not in the register changes nothing; the answer may say so, without setting the conflict field.

question: What's the shortest password the Mirrowfen directory will let me set?
reference_answer: Mirrowfen passwords must be at least 16 characters long (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 3.1).

question: Does Mirrowfen make me change my password on a fixed timetable, or only in certain situations?
reference_answer: Mirrowfen passwords do not expire on a schedule: a password is changed only when compromise is known or suspected (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 3.3).

question: I keep mistyping my Mirrowfen password. When does the directory lock me out, and do I have to call someone to get back in?
reference_answer: An account locks for 15 minutes after 8 failed sign-in attempts and unlocks by itself when the lockout ends, so no call is needed (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 4.1).

question: A Mirrowfen account was disabled this morning. For how long could its registered MFA factors still work?
reference_answer: MFA factors are revoked within 24 hours of the account being disabled, and a revoked factor cannot be used again (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 6.1).

question: Apart from the daily re-prompt, when else will a Mirrowfen sign-in ask me for MFA again?
reference_answer: Mirrowfen sign-ins ask for MFA again after 24 hours, and also after you sign out and when you sign in from a new device or browser (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 7.1).

question: Which authenticator methods does Mirrowfen approve as second factors for my account?
reference_answer: Mirrowfen's approved factors are authenticator app push notifications with number matching, authenticator app one-time codes and FIDO2 security keys (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 3.1).

question: I've just been given a Mirrowfen administrator account. Is there a particular second factor I have to use with it?
reference_answer: Yes: Mirrowfen administrators use a FIDO2 security key, for every sign-in with an administrator account (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 4).

question: Do my Mirrowfen passwords need a mix of numbers, symbols and capital letters?
reference_answer: No: Mirrowfen does not impose composition rules. New passwords are checked against a blocklist of common and breached passwords, and a password on the blocklist is rejected (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 3.2).

question: Who should I contact at Mirrowfen when I can't sign in or need help with my password?
reference_answer: Contact Mirrowfen IT Support, whose email address and phone number are given in the Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 6, for help with passwords or sign-in problems. A team contact is answered, not refused.

question: Can I tell my teammate my Mirrowfen password so she can finish my report while I'm on holiday?
reference_answer: No: never share your Mirrowfen password with anyone. If a colleague needs access to a system, they ask for their own account and never use yours (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 5).

question: A colleague has offered to approve my Mirrowfen sign-in prompts on his phone while I'm in meetings. Can I add his phone as one of my factors?
reference_answer: No: register your own factors in the identity portal and never share them with anyone (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 3.1). Register an approved factor of your own instead.

question: Can I use my Mirrowfen password for my personal shopping accounts too, so I only have one to remember?
reference_answer: No: do not reuse a Mirrowfen password for any other account, work or personal. Store work passwords only in the approved password manager (Mirrowfen Password Standard, section 5).

question: For a board paper on password expiry: what is our rule, and do the two outside guidance excerpts in the pack support it?
reference_answer: Halvenroot requires user passwords to expire every 60 days (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4). NIST SP 800-63B-4 (section 3.1.1.2) says verifiers shall not require subscribers to change passwords periodically, and the NCSC (section 3 of its excerpt) says regular password changing harms rather than improves security. The company rule applies to Halvenroot staff, and the difference is flagged.

question: A new hire quoted the UK cyber security centre's view that forcing staff to change passwords regularly does more harm than good. Is our expiry rule in line with that?
reference_answer: No: Halvenroot requires user passwords to expire every 60 days (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4), while the NCSC (section 3 of its excerpt) advises against regular password expiry. The company rule applies to Halvenroot staff, and the difference is flagged.

question: Does our lockout threshold for standard accounts fit within the limit NIST's guidance puts on failed attempts?
reference_answer: Yes: NIST SP 800-63B-4 (section 3.2.2) limits consecutive failed attempts to no more than 100 and says that limit is an upper bound that may be set lower; Halvenroot locks a standard account after 10 failed sign-in attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1). 100 is NIST's bound, never the company limit.

question: If an auditor asks whether our lockout setting follows the NCSC's recommendation on login attempts, what do I tell them?
reference_answer: That it does: the NCSC recommends allowing between 5 and 10 login attempts before the account is frozen, if lockout is used (NCSC excerpt, section 1), and Halvenroot locks a standard account after 10 failed sign-in attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1), within that range. The range is attributed to the NCSC, never stated as the company rule.

question: Which document actually sets how often privileged accounts are reviewed, and what is the interval?
reference_answer: Privileged accounts are reviewed every 30 days, set in the Access Review Procedure, section 3.2; the Privileged Access Standard, section 8.1, points there for the frequency.

question: An app team asks whether the secret of their integration's service account must be renewed as often as staff passwords. How often is it rotated?
reference_answer: No: service account credentials are not user passwords and follow the Privileged Access Standard (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4); service account secrets are kept in the secrets vault and rotated every 180 days (Privileged Access Standard, section 7.2), so the 60-day user expiry does not apply.

question: Our integration service account can administer the identity platform. Which lockout values from the password standard apply to it, and who unlocks it?
reference_answer: A service account with any of the glossary's privileged rights, such as administering the identity platform, is also a privileged account (Halvenroot Security Glossary, section 10), so the privileged column of Table 1 applies: it locks after 5 failed sign-in attempts and stays locked until the IAM team unlocks it (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1).

question: A new warehouse supervisor starts in a fortnight. When HR works out its notice to IAM, which days count, and how many of them does it need?
reference_answer: HR must notify the IAM team at least 5 business days before the start date (Account Lifecycle Policy, section 3.1), and a business day is Monday to Friday, excluding Halvenroot public holidays (Halvenroot Security Glossary, section 4), so weekends and public holidays do not count.

question: I'm new to the SOC rota. Once a compromise is confirmed, which containment steps do I carry out on the account, and does the order matter?
reference_answer: Yes, the order matters: carry out the six containment steps in this order and record each one: (1) disable sign-in for the account; (2) revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens; (3) revoke all registered MFA factors; (4) reset the password; (5) check mailbox forwarding rules and remove any that the account holder did not create; (6) for a privileged account, also rotate every secret the account could read (Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, sections 5 and 5.1 to 5.6).

question: A warehouse employee resigns on the spot and HR files the leaver notification at 09:30. How long can the account stay enabled, and when must the MFA factors be gone by?
reference_answer: If an employee leaves with immediate effect, the account is disabled within 2 hours of HR's leaver notification (Account Lifecycle Policy, section 5.1), so by 11:30; all MFA factors are revoked within 1 hour of the account being disabled (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 6.1), so they are gone by 12:30 at the latest.

question: I'm covering the network on-call shift from my personal computer tonight. Can I keep the VPN open while idle for hours, like the rest of the rota does?
reference_answer: No: the rota's exception, whose Status in the exceptions register is Approved, allows VPN sessions to stay open for up to 4 hours of inactivity until 2027-01-31 only from Halvenroot-managed on-call laptops, with the SOC monitoring those sessions (Policy Exceptions Process, Table 1 and section 5.2). From a personal computer the exception does not apply, and VPN sessions disconnect after 60 minutes of inactivity (Remote Access Policy, section 4.5).

question: I've lost the FIDO2 key for my admin account and I'm on call tonight. Can I use one of the break-glass accounts to get into the consoles instead?
reference_answer: No: a break-glass account may be used only while an outage of the MFA or SSO service has been declared (Privileged Access Standard, section 6.3), and there is no other way to sign in without MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 5.3). For a lost security key, contact the IT Service Desk: after a video-call identity check it issues a temporary access pass to register a new factor (section 5.1; Identity and Access FAQ, Q4).

question: I need to hand a large file to a supplier on a USB stick. Can I get my laptop to accept the stick despite the block?
reference_answer: No: USB storage devices are blocked on Halvenroot devices, and users must not try to work around the block (Device Policy, section 6.1). If the work genuinely needs removable media, exceptions follow the Policy Exceptions Process (section 6.2; Identity and Access FAQ, Q7): submit a Security Exception Request in the IT portal (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.1).

question: My phone with the Mirrowfen authenticator died this morning. Could IT Support simply disable MFA for me until the replacement arrives?
reference_answer: No: MFA is required for every sign-in to Mirrowfen systems (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 2). Call Mirrowfen IT Support instead: after checking your identity, it issues a one-time recovery code, valid for 2 hours, to sign in once and register a new factor (section 5.1).

question: Our auditors want data handed over on encrypted USB drives again this year. How do we ask for an exception to the USB block, and who has to approve it?
reference_answer: Submit a Security Exception Request in the IT portal, stating the rule, the reason, the compensating controls and the end date (Policy Exceptions Process, section 3.1); the line manager, the resource owner and the CISO must all approve it (section 3.2; Identity and Access FAQ, Q11). Asking how to request an exception is the sanctioned route, not a bypass, so it is answered, not refused.

question: During containment of a compromised account, am I as the SOC analyst allowed to remove all of the user's MFA methods, and which documents back that up?
reference_answer: Yes: revoking all registered MFA factors is containment step 5.3 of the Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, and the Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 6.2, confirms that factors are revoked when the Security Operations Centre contains a compromised account. It is a sanctioned containment step, not a way around MFA, so it is answered.

reference_answer: Passwords must be at least 15 characters long under version 2.0, which is current (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.1). Version 1.0 required at least 12 characters (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.1) and is superseded.

question: Did the original password standard insist on different kinds of characters, and is that still required?
reference_answer: Version 1.0, now superseded, required at least one upper-case letter, one lower-case letter, one digit and one symbol (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.2). The current version 2.0 imposes no composition rules; new passwords are checked against a blocklist of common and breached passwords instead (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.3).

question: How many failed sign-ins locked an account under version 1.0 of the password standard, and how many does it take for a standard account today?
reference_answer: Version 1.0, now superseded, locked accounts after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.4). Under the current version 2.0, a standard account locks after 10 failed sign-in attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1).

question: I need both figures for an audit: has the password change interval always been what it is today, or did the original standard set a different one?
reference_answer: User passwords expire every 60 days under version 2.0, which is current (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4). Version 1.0 said every 90 days (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.3) and is superseded.

question: A legacy app's lockout threshold was copied from our first password standard. What did that version require, and what does the current standard set for normal accounts?
reference_answer: Version 1.0, which is superseded, locked accounts after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts (Password Standard 1.0, section 4.4). The current version 2.0 locks a standard account after 10 failed sign-in attempts (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 5, Table 1), and that is the rule.

question: Under the password rules in force today, must my new password include an upper-case letter and a symbol?
reference_answer: No: Halvenroot does not impose composition rules (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.3); new passwords are checked against a blocklist of common and breached passwords. Version 1.0's character-mix rule is superseded and is never given as the rule.

question: I'm writing the joiner checklist. Which minimum password length should it quote from the standard that's in force?
reference_answer: Passwords must be at least 15 characters long (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.1). Version 1.0's 12 characters is superseded and is never given as the rule.

question: For the audit trail: on what date did the current password standard replace version 1.0, and when had version 1.0 itself taken effect?
reference_answer: Version 2.0 of the Password and Authentication Standard took effect on 2025-09-01 and replaced version 1.0, which had taken effect on 2024-03-01 (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, sections 1 and 9). Which document is current comes from the register, not from these dates.

question: isn't making us change passwords every couple of months exactly what NIST tells organisations not to do?
reference_answer: Halvenroot requires user passwords to expire every 60 days (Password and Authentication Standard 2.0, section 4.4); NIST SP 800-63B-4 (section 3.1.1.2) says verifiers shall not require subscribers to change passwords periodically. The company rule applies to Halvenroot staff, and the difference is flagged.

question: my teammate lost her security key on the train - can she just borrow mine to sign in until IT sorts her out?
reference_answer: No: never share a factor with a colleague (Multi-Factor Authentication Standard, section 3.3). She contacts the IT Service Desk, which verifies her identity on a video call and issues her a temporary access pass to register a new factor (section 5.1; Identity and Access FAQ, Q4).

question: account's definitely been popped and i'm the soc analyst on shift. how do i lock it down, step by step?
reference_answer: Carry out the six containment steps in this order and record each one: (1) disable sign-in for the account; (2) revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens; (3) revoke all registered MFA factors; (4) reset the password; (5) check mailbox forwarding rules and remove any that the account holder did not create; (6) for a privileged account, also rotate every secret the account could read (Account-Compromise Incident Runbook, sections 5 and 5.1 to 5.6).

question: can i use txt mesage codes for my mirrowfen mfa if the authenticater app isnt working?
reference_answer: Yes, but only as a fallback: SMS codes are allowed only as a fallback factor, when no other approved factor is available (Mirrowfen MFA Standard, section 3.2), so register an approved factor as soon as you can.
